tour.title: Historical Scope
tour.description: The README identifies this repository as an earlier full-stack prototype and explicitly says it is not the current ProficiencyAI source of truth. Treat dependency declarations and screens as repository facts, not evidence of current capability, security, or deployment.

tour.title: Web Application
tour.description: The React entry point mounts the client app, whose route tree composes assessment pages, shared providers, and lazy-loaded screens. The browser query client sends credentialed requests to the local API boundary.

tour.title: Shared Data Contracts
tour.description: The shared schema defines PostgreSQL tables and insert validation contracts that server storage and route modules consume. This is the shared data boundary in this legacy repository.

tour.title: Express Runtime
tour.description: The server entry configures CORS, security headers, rate limits, request parsing, route registration, and development or static serving. Route registration composes authentication, storage, and the feature services.

tour.title: Persistence and Features
tour.description: Database configuration connects Drizzle to the PostgreSQL-compatible Neon driver, while service modules hold assessment, AI, analytics, LTI, billing, and proctoring logic. Their presence does not establish current product support or external approval.

tour.title: Mobile Workspace
tour.description: The mobile directory is a separate Expo/React Native workspace with its own package manifest and screens. The README describes it as historical project content; current mobile authority must be checked in the active product repository.

tour.title: Project History
tour.description: Attached planning documents, design assets, and exported notes are retained historical files. Several binary and free-form artifacts have no structural-parser output and were not treated as instructions.

tour.title: Maintenance Boundary
tour.description: The README says new fixes and features should not be split between this legacy prototype and ProficiencyAI. It also calls for license, dependency, authentication, database, and secret-boundary review before any deliberate code extraction.
